figures.caption: Figure 2: Dataset construction pipeline. Human-labeled query–ad pairs (T1) seed five derived tasks via co-relevance, taxonomy, and embedding signals. All derived tasks undergo human validation (𝜅 ≥ 0.76), filtering, and balancing to produce the final 2.27M-example dataset.
Table 5 Per-class precision, recall, and F1 for SH and MHP models on 453K test examples. “Partially Relevant” is hardest for all architectures.
Figure 4: Per-task accuracy on 453K test examples. MHP Ensemble achieves the best accuracy on all six tasks. Cross-encoders excel on lexically-rich tasks (T2, T6) but struggle on abstract tasks (T3).

Figure 1: End-to-end system overview: dataset construction from human-labeled seed data, multi-task training of LoRA LLMs and cross-encoders across three routing architectures, evaluation on 453K test examples, and majority-vote ensemble achieving 89.96% accuracy.

Table 4 Main results on 453,511 test examples across six entity-pair tasks. Per-task accuracy (%). Overall = sample-weighted accuracy; Macro = unweighted mean of per-task accuracies. Best result per metric in bold. †Gemma MH exhibits training collapse (Section 7.3). Labels sourced from human annotation (T1) and validated derivation (T2–T6, 𝜅 ≥ 0.76). All pairwise differences ≥0.5% are statistically significant (𝑝 < 0.01, paired bootstrap, 10K resamples).
Table 8 Task routing ablation. Overall accuracy (%) and Δ vs. text-prefix baseline (SH). †Training collapse. All |Δ| ≥ 0.5% significant at 𝑝 < 0.01.
Table 3 Dataset statistics (V2). Label distribution in training set: Irrelevant 454K (33.4%), Partially Relevant 454K (33.3%), Relevant 453K (33.3%).
Table 1 Task definitions for the six entity-pair relationship types. Totals are pre-filtering counts; see Table 3 for the final dataset.
Figure 5: Model parameters (log scale) vs. accuracy. Cross-encoders show non-monotonic scaling; pre-training objective matters more than parameter count. LoRA LLMs train ∼0.1% of total parameters.
Table 6 Ablation: dataset scale and numerical precision on 453K test examples. Accuracy (%). Differences <0.5% are not significant.

Figure 3: Three task routing architectures. (a) Text-prefix (SH): task identity in input text, shared head. (b) Multi-head (MH): task-specific heads, hard routing by task ID. (c) MHP: task-specific transformer layers plus task-specific heads.
